back: Embed what is read together and bounded; reference what is unbounded or changes at a different rate. Keyword: access patterns first.

front: Multiple entity types in one container
back: Normal and often desirable, distinguished by a type property — a container is a unit of throughput, not a table. Keyword: not a table.
Expires documents automatically at container or item level — how a session or telemetry store stays bounded. Keyword: self-cleaning.
Documents written years apart coexist; a version property plus version-aware readers is what stops old shapes breaking. Keyword: no migration event.
It cannot be changed on an existing container — correcting it means a new container and a migration. Keyword: get it right first.
High cardinality, even spread of storage and requests, and present in the common queries. Keyword: all three.
20 GB — so a key whose values group too much data hits a ceiling regardless of throughput. Keyword: storage cap.
One physical partition taking a disproportionate share of requests, throttling while the account looks under-used. Keyword: throughput is divided.
Worst case for writes — every write lands in the same partition. Keyword: never for write-heavy.
Concatenates fields to raise cardinality when no single property spreads well. Keyword: build a better key.
Up to three levels; a query supplying only the first level still targets efficiently while storage subdivides beneath. Keyword: three levels.
Stored procedures and transactional batch work within one logical partition only. Keyword: same partition key value.
Scales between 10% of the maximum and the maximum, billing for what is used. Dearer per RU at sustained full load. Keyword: spiky workloads.
No provisioning and per-operation billing, but lower limits and no throughput SLA. Keyword: dev and intermittent.
Direct connects to replicas over TCP with lowest latency; gateway routes over HTTPS for restricted networks. Keyword: latency vs firewalls.
Create the client once and reuse it — one per request exhausts connections and adds latency to every call. Keyword: classic defect.
A point read by id and partition key is the cheapest operation. A query costs more even returning one document. Keyword: know both keys.
Use the document ETag with an if-match condition so a concurrent write fails instead of silently overwriting. Keyword: ETag.
The default; guarantees a client reads its own writes. Usually the right answer. Keyword: read your own writes.
Not available with multi-region writes, and costs latency and RUs. Keyword: single write region only.
Conflicts cannot arise with one write region. Resolve with last-writer-wins or a custom procedure. Keyword: the cost of writing everywhere.
Automatic promotes on regional failure by priority. Manual moves the write region deliberately, for planned migration. Keyword: unplanned vs planned.
A column-oriented copy isolated from the transactional workload, so reporting consumes no transactional RUs. Keyword: isolation.
Mirroring replicates into OneLake for Fabric with no code. The Spark connector is for processing in Spark. Keyword: destination decides.
It records creates and updates only — use a soft-delete flag with TTL to make deletions visible. Keyword: soft delete.
Referential integrity is enforced by the application, typically through change feed reacting to changes. Keyword: enforce it yourself.
Every response carries the RU cost of the operation — more informative than any estimate. Keyword: read the header.
Omitting the partition key fans the query out to every physical partition. Sometimes correct, expensive by default. Keyword: supply the key.
Serves repeated point reads and queries at no RU cost. Needs gateway mode and a dedicated gateway. Keyword: repeated identical reads.
Great for reads, expensive for writes. Excluding unused paths is a direct cost decision. Keyword: exclude for write-heavy.
Required for ORDER BY across two or more properties, and order-sensitive — (a ASC, b DESC) does not serve the reverse. Keyword: direction matters.
Applied in the background; the container stays queryable and performance improves when the transformation finishes. Keyword: not instant.
How the change feed processor distributes work; it is a real container needing its own throughput. Keyword: provision the leases.
Reports how far behind the processor is — a growing backlog means consumption is slower than production. Keyword: measure the lag.
More instances than partition ranges achieves nothing. Keyword: scale to the ranges.

front: Change feed processing must be idempotent
back: A change can be delivered more than once when leases move between instances. Keyword: at-least-once.
Rate limited for exceeding provisioned throughput, with a retry-after the SDK honours. A capacity signal, not an outage. Keyword: expected.
A failed precondition — the ETag did not match, so optimistic concurrency prevented an overwrite. Keyword: someone else wrote first.
Utilisation of the busiest physical partition, not an average — which is how a hot partition shows itself. Keyword: the busiest one.
Separates the service's contribution from the client's and the network's. Keyword: whose fault.
Requires a support request, so recovery time is not entirely in your hands. Keyword: raise a ticket.
Point-in-time restore to any second within 7 or 30 days, performed by the account owner. Keyword: self-service PITR.
Recovery includes a cutover step; the existing account is never overwritten. Keyword: new account.
You can switch to continuous backup but not back again. Keyword: decide once.
Azure RBAC governs creating containers and changing throughput. Data plane RBAC or account keys govern reading documents. Keyword: two planes.
Shared secrets granting full data access. Prefer Entra-based data plane RBAC and disable key access entirely. Keyword: attribute the access.
Held in Key Vault where the organisation must own them — losing key access makes the data inaccessible. Keyword: your key, your risk.
Batches operations under the covers to maximise ingestion throughput from the SDK. Keyword: large loads.
Hold it in ARM or Bicep, because a manual change in production is invisible afterwards. Keyword: declare it.
Standard to autoscale and back is an imperative operation via PowerShell or CLI. Keyword: scripted, not declared.
